subject: Chemistry
text: (a) Explain, in terms of electrons, with a diagram how a flame test works. (3 marks) (b) Explain the difference between an emission spectra and absorption spectra. (4 marks)
html:
(a) Explain, in terms of electrons, with a diagram how a flame test works. (3 marks)

(b) Explain the difference between an emission spectra and absorption spectra. (4 marks)
answerHtml:
Source marks require teacher review. Paper allocates 3 marks to part (a), but the supplied guide allocates 2; total paper marks 7 retained.

(a) Explain, in terms of electrons, with a diagram how a flame test works. (2 marks)

CORRECT DIAGRAM [1]

Heat is applied to the sample [extra]

Electrons “transform” specific wavelengths of light to kinetic energy and jump to the next energy level. (become excited) [1]

This energy is then released as a different wavelength of light [1] and is specific to the element as quantum jumps are essential [extra].

(b) Explain the difference between an emission spectra and absorption spectra. (4 marks)

Emission spectra – a sample of atoms absorb energy [1] and excited electrons release/transform their energy into light energy [1]

Absorption spectra – a whole spectrum of light wavelengths are shone on a sample of vapourised atoms that absorb specific wavelengths of light energy. [1] These absorbed wavelengths of light are identified as missing or black marks on the spectrum [1]

subject: Chemistry
text: (a) What is electronegativity? (1 mark) (b) Explain what happens to electronegativity as you go across the Periodic Table, from left to right in the second period? (2 marks) (c) Explain in terms of electrostatics, the trend in electonegativity that you stated in part (b). (2 marks) (d) Define ionisation energy, and explain the trend of the group 2 elements as you go down the group. (3 marks) (e) Explain what happens to the atomic radius of the elements as you go across period 2. (2 marks)
html:
(a) What is electronegativity? (1 mark)

(b) Explain what happens to electronegativity as you go across the Periodic Table, from left to right in the second period? (2 marks)

(c) Explain in terms of electrostatics, the trend in electonegativity that you stated in part (b).

(2 marks)

(d) Define ionisation energy, and explain the trend of the group 2 elements as you go down the group. (3 marks)

(e) Explain what happens to the atomic radius of the elements as you go across period 2.

(2 marks)
answerHtml:
(a) What is electronegativity? (1 mark)

The tendency/ability for an element to attract electrons.

(b) Explain what happens to electronegativity as you go across the Periodic Table, from left to right in the second period? (2 marks)

Electronegativity increases moving left to right [1] due to the increased nuclear charge [1]

(c) Explain in terms of electrostatics, the trend in electronegativity that you stated in part (b).

(2 marks)

The center of each consecutive atom has in increased positive charge due to an increased number of protons in the nucleus. [1]

As a result, it has more affinity to attract electrons. [1]

(d) Define ionisation energy, and explain the trend of the group 2 elements as you go down the group. (3 marks)

Ionisation energy is the energy required to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of an element. (ie from the outermost electron energy levels) [1]

Ionisation energy decreases [1] as you go down group 2 because of electron screening/shielding. This negates the attraction from the increasingly positive nucleus. [1]

(e) Explain what happens to the atomic radius of the elements as you go across period 2.

(2 marks)

Atomic radius decreases as you go across period 2. [1] this is due to the increased nuclear charge pulling on the electrons inwards. [1]
